about: Browser mission of 2026-11-12 (local date; 16:13-16:59 PST): tests/browser/mission/lunar-direct.spec.ts at commit 2a9bb7d, one flight, pad to splashdown, flown by the test pilot in the page through the controls; 36 picture stops, 40 pictures in out/screens/mission/. The windows and the phase log of the full record (out/mission/browser-mission.json) are left out here; `windowsOverTheLines` and `comparison` are computed from them and from browser-mission-2026-11-11.json.

pictureReadings.shows: The stack at the umbilical tower from above, the pad's apron, lava plain, the coast and the sea with the sun's glitter, cumulus; launch panel (plane crossing T- 2:21), warp x50 while the pilot waits for the window.
The frame of lift-off (T+0, 19.1 m): the launch cloud rolling out left and right of the pad, the stack still beside the tower, toast "Lift-off".
pictureReadings.wrong: No flame is visible in this frame: the base of the vehicle is behind the pad's structure and the HUD's navball.

pictureReadings.shows: 14.9 km, Mach 1.67: the stack from behind and below, the plume at the lower edge behind the navball, cloud field and sea far below.
pictureReadings.wrong: In the sun's glint on the sea (lower right) a pair of pale meandering ribbons and several fans of dark parallel arcs: drawn-looking lines, not water (checked in a crop at full resolution).

pictureReadings.shows: 77.1 km: the first stage just free, a white flash at the gap, the second stage and spacecraft ahead; the Earth's limb with a thin blue line of air, cloud field.
Half a second later: the first stage a few metres behind, the second stage's engine glowing.
Two seconds later: the first stage a length and a half behind and below, the second stage's plume a pale cone.
96.0 km: a small glow at the nose (the tower's motors), the second stage burning, the spent first stage a speck at the lower left.
The four fairing petals opening around the spacecraft, the tower leaving ahead on its motor's flame.
The four petals tumbling away on all sides, lander and capsule exposed on top of the second stage.
183.8 km, in orbit: the second stage's tank just apart from the third stage and spacecraft, no plume, cloud field below, stars above the limb.
The second stage half a metre apart.
The second stage two metres apart, the third stage's engine visible in the open ring.
The same instant as the stage separation (0.1 s later), toasts "M-2 separation" and "Earth orbit".
The pilot's couch: panel, caution lights and the three displays legible (flight, orbit, systems), the cabin evenly lit.
pictureReadings.wrong: Both forward windows are a flat light grey with faint scratches. The Sun stands in the windows (frame position -0.08, 0.27): no sun disc, no bloom, no Earth or sky can be made out. (The stack flies heads-up here; the heads-down picture with the Earth in the windows is the app spec's leo-cockpit.png.)

pictureReadings.shows: 299.9 km at cut-off: the third stage and spacecraft, two RCS jets at the tail, cloud field and limb below, toast "TLI complete", burn panel with 0.6 m/s remaining.
64.4 Mm from the Moon: the lander stack sunlit from the side against black; a small gibbous Earth (blue and white at full resolution) at the lower left.
pictureReadings.wrong: The Moon, 64 Mm ahead, is not in the frame.

pictureReadings.shows: 104.7 km over the Moon: the stack from behind (the descent engine's bell and truss), RCS puffs, the grey surface below with a sharp limb, toast "Lunar orbit".
pictureReadings.wrong: To judge: from this height the surface is smooth, with few craters to be seen.

pictureReadings.shows: 30 m, 4.4 m/s down: the lander with its gear down over the mare, its shadow far to the left, black sky, sharp horizon.
pictureReadings.wrong: No engine plume and no dust (throttle 21 %). The small craters farther off read as flat dark ovals.

pictureReadings.shows: 10 m, 1.5 m/s down: the shadow nearer.
pictureReadings.wrong: No dust at 10 m (throttle 15 %), no plume.

pictureReadings.shows: 3 m, 1.0 m/s down: the shadow reaches the lander's feet.
pictureReadings.wrong: No dust, no plume (throttle 12 %).

pictureReadings.shows: The first footpad on the ground (panel "LANDED"), throttle still 12 %.
pictureReadings.wrong: No dust at the contact.

pictureReadings.shows: One second later: engine off, the lander at rest on its four legs.
At rest 0.8 m from the target in Mare Tranquillitatis: long shadow to the left, a small crater with rocks in the foreground, toast "Lunar touchdown".
The cabin on the Moon, lit; displays legible (the orbit page reads "Moon - landed - no orbit").
pictureReadings.wrong: The forward windows are plain black: they look at the sky; the Earth is in the frame's lower part, behind the panel.

pictureReadings.shows: 50 m up at 13 m/s: the ascent stage and capsule, framed closer (the vessel is smaller now), the mare below, darker than in the landing pictures (EV100 14.2 against 12.8).
pictureReadings.wrong: No plume under the ascent engine at 100 % throttle, no dust; the descent stage left behind is not in the frame.

pictureReadings.shows: 359.7 Mm from the Earth: the ascent stage and capsule sunlit, the Moon a small full disc at the lower left.

The stage from its shadowed side, RCS jets with a wide grey haze around them, a small gibbous Earth at the lower left, the capsule's nose catching the light at the lower right; toast "Entry corridor targeted".
pictureReadings.wrong: To judge: the haze of the RCS jets is as wide as the vehicle.

pictureReadings.shows: 122.0 km, 10.8 km/s, at night: the capsule alone, dark, faintly lit from one side, heat shield forward; entry panel (14 kW/m^2).
pictureReadings.wrong: The Earth below is black (night side): nothing but the capsule in the frame.

pictureReadings.shows: 60.0 km, 2.47 MW/m^2, 4.8 g: a white to pale pink sheath wrapped round the heat shield with a long pale wake, the capsule dark inside it.
pictureReadings.wrong: To judge: the glow is nearly white (little colour), and the capsule's flank carries a pattern of light streaks. The recovery panel reads "Central Atlantic, 13.92 Mm" in this frame and "Central Pacific" before and after.

pictureReadings.shows: The couch during the peak: the cabin dim, displays legible (4.78 g, 60.0 km), caution lights SAS, RCS, COMM BLK and LIFT UP lit.
pictureReadings.wrong: Both windows are a flat light grey: no structure, no flicker, no colour of the plasma, and the cabin walls are not tinted by it.

pictureReadings.shows: 54.6 km, 5.58 g, 901 kW/m^2: a white-pink glow as wide as the frame.
pictureReadings.wrong: The capsule is burnt out to white inside the glow, its detail gone: the exposure stands at EV100 7.7 here (16.5 at the peak of the heating 44 s earlier).

pictureReadings.shows: 7.4 km, 132 m/s, low sun: the capsule tan in the warm light, one riser running up out of the frame, pink cumulus and a grey sea in haze below.
pictureReadings.wrong: The drogues are above the frame: only the riser shows. A pale vertical streak hangs below the capsule.

pictureReadings.shows: Three seconds later, 99 m/s: two risers running up.
pictureReadings.wrong: The canopies are above the frame.

pictureReadings.shows: 3.2 km, 50 m/s: the capsule under one riser, cumulus in sunset colours, the sea a flat purple-grey.
pictureReadings.wrong: The mains are above the frame.

pictureReadings.shows: Eight seconds later, 18 m/s: three risers.
pictureReadings.wrong: The canopies are above the frame: no picture of this flight shows an open chute.

pictureReadings.shows: The capsule in the water, a crown of white spray with flying drops around it, a ring of foam, dark blue swell, warm clouds at the horizon.
pictureReadings.wrong: A box-shaped darker patch on the water in front of the capsule, with straight vertical edges.

pictureReadings.shows: The crown at its largest, a sheet of spray, the foam patch spreading; the capsule hidden in the spray.
pictureReadings.wrong: Patches of turquoise speckles on the water at the lower left; some spray drops are drawn as long straight lines.

pictureReadings.shows: The capsule afloat, dark brown, upright; a wide patch of foam with dark holes over the swell, tinted pink by the low sun; a main canopy (orange and white gores) coming down at the left with its risers taut.
pictureReadings.wrong: To judge: the foam patch fills the lower half of the frame. The canopy stands on the water like a flat fan.

pictureReadings.shows: The foam thinner and broken up (the patch has aged), the capsule upright, panel "SPLASHED", the sea very dark under the low sun.
pictureReadings.wrong: The box-shaped darker patch in front of the capsule again; the canopy still stands as a fan at the left edge.

pictureReadings.shows: 34 s after the splash: the capsule riding upright in what is left of the foam, toast "Splashdown".
pictureReadings.wrong: The box-shaped darker patch in front of the capsule (edges about a capsule's width apart, from the waterline down); the fan-shaped canopy.

frameIntervalLine.line: ARCHITECTURE 29 as restated by the lead on 2026-11-12 (commit 9a873e0): per phase, against the measured harness clock, the median frame interval within 1 % of the nominal period; dropped frames (an interval over 1.5 periods) at most 0.5 % of the phase's frames; no frame of 33 ms or more.
frameIntervalLine.judged: offline on 2026-11-12 from out/mission/browser-mission.json, without a new flight
frameIntervalLine.basis: What the flight recorded per window (711 windows of up to 241 frames): the render core's frame-to-frame statistics p50, p99, max and its count of 33 ms or more, not the intervals. A phase's median lies between the smallest and the largest of its windows' medians; the dropped frames of a window are bounded by its max and p99 (in every window with an interval over 1.5 periods the p99 is under it, so the window has 1 or, with 240 frames, at most 2 of them). The core takes its time stamp where the frame is drawn; from the next flight on the spec judges the requestAnimationFrame time stamps themselves (src/app/frameIntervals.ts).
